want.now.why: quero takes a bare infinitive, no 'to' and no preposition. Language names go without an article after aprender: khasi, not o khasi.

want.past.why: Tense sits on the door: queria is the imperfeito, the normal past for a wish. Eu quis aprender would mean I decided or tried to.

want.neg.why: No do-support: não simply goes in front of the conjugated verb. Speech often doubles it: eu não quero aprender khasi, não.

want.q.why: Nothing moves and no question word is added: the statement order stays and rising pitch alone makes it a question.

decline.now.why: Declining an invitation uses ir (go), not vir (come): you go to where the other person is. tenho que is the everyday have to.

decline.past.why: Both doors take the pretérito perfeito (pude, tive), one-off events. Speech often uses não consegui ir, I didn't manage to go.

decline.fut.why: vou + infinitive carries the future in both halves, so poder and ter que become infinitives. The second eu is dropped: vou already says I.

decline.although.why: mesmo que forces the subjunctive: tenha instead of tenho. Word order stays the same as in a main clause, unlike German.

like.now.why: gostar always needs de before the thing liked: gosto de café. No article for coffee in general.

like.neg.why: não goes before gosto and nothing else changes; de stays glued to the verb in the negative too.

like.she.why: gosto becomes gosta: the verb ending shows the person, -o for eu and -a for ela (and for você).

like.q.why: Same order as the statement; intonation makes the question. você takes the same verb form as ela: gosta.

go.habit.why: a + o fuses into ao. Speech in Brazil usually says vou no mercado, with em instead of a, though schools call it wrong.

go.prog.why: A real progressive, estar + gerund, shaped like English am going. In speech estou shrinks to tô: tô indo ao mercado.

go.past.why: One word carries go and past: fui. It is also the past of ser (to be), so eu fui can mean I went or I was.

go.fut.why: Plain present plus amanhã: the usual future of ir is not vou ir. Eu irei ao mercado is correct but sounds written.

go.neg.why: não comes before the auxiliary, not between estou and indo: the whole progressive is negated from the front.

live.now.why: Present moro plus há (it has been) two years. Speech often flips it: faz dois anos que eu moro aqui.

live.past.why: Finished period: pretérito perfeito morei, and há changes to por. Speech often drops it: morei lá dois anos.

live.fut.why: No future perfect: the future goes on vai fazer (it will make), que links, and morar stays in the present.

live.q.why: The question opens with faz quanto tempo (how long does it make) and que; mora stays plain present. Há quanto tempo você mora aqui? also works.

if.real.why: se + future subjunctive tiver, a form English lacks. Se eu tenho tempo sounds foreign here. Main clause: vou + infinitive.

if.unreal.why: Past subjunctive tivesse, conditional viajaria. Everyday Brazilian speech often swaps in the imperfeito: eu viajava.

if.past.why: Both halves are ter + participle: tivesse tido, teria viajado. Speech often says eu tinha viajado for the second half.
